title.narrative: National -Lund-KTH Univ -Sust fishing in Colombia Open Innovation- 2020-2024
National -Lund-KTH Univ-Hållbart fiske genom Öppen Innovation Colombia 2020-2024

description.narrative: Målet med detta projektstöd är att stärka och utveckla kapaciteten för kommunitära ekosystem genom en hållbar fiskerimodell som bygger på öppen innovation och medskapande, som syftar till att bidra till en minskning av den miljömässiga och ekonomiska påverkan som det nuvarande systemet med fossila bränslen ger upphov till. Stödet ges till tre avtalsparter: Colombias nationella universitet (UNAL), Caucas Universitet, Lunds universitet och Kungliga tekniska högskolan (KTH). Målgruppen bor i Guapi, ett konfliktdrabbat område i Colombia.

The general objective of this project support is to strengthen and develop communitarian ecosystem capabilities and self-efficacy by designing a sustainable fishing model under open innovation and co-creation methodologies that contributes to reducing the environmental and economic impact generated by the current fossil fuel system. The support is provided to three agreement partners: the National University of Colombia (UNAL), University of Cauca, Lund University, and the Royal Institute of Technology (KTH). The target population lives in Guapi, a conflict-affected area in Colombia.

The general objective of the contribution is “to strength and develop communitarian ecosystem capabilities and self-efficacy by designing a sustainable fishing model under open innovation and co-creation methodologies that contributes to reducing the environmental and economic impact generated by the current fossil fuel system”. It is expected that through the development of this project, a more dynamic economy and greater investment from the private and public sectors will lead, in the long term, to an improvement in the quality of life for people living in the municipality of Guapi. It is also expected to stimulate other related initiatives that contribute to the development of artisanal fishing in sustainable terms, such as tourism. The specific proposed outputs are -To develop a sustainable model associated with to the artisanal fishing value chain in Guapi through identifying socioeconomic and environmental factors of the ecosystem. -To design and build a boat powered by renewable and hybrid energies in coordination with the designed sustainable fishing model. - To propose a business plan in coordination with social entrepreneurships, strengthening the proposed sustainable fishing model.

description.narrative:
The first outcome of developing a sustainable model linked to the artisanal fishing value chain in Guapi, as well as the the third outcome of proposing a business plan linked to social entrepreneurships, were fully completed in 2024. The second outcome of designing and building a boat powered by renewable and hybrid energies, has reached 85% of implementation and will be completed in 2025.
For the first outcome of developing a sustainable model linked to the artisanal fishing value chain in Guapi, the analysis of the fishing value creation has continued in partnership with the participants fishing organizations. The value chain concept was changed by value creation, recognizing the value of the community organization, of the traditional knowledge, of the communities in the territory, of the forms of teaching and learning expressed through music, literature, in their relationship with the river, in food culture, that is in their daily practices. Local traditional knowledge and practices are fundamental in the processes of preserving biodiversity (environmental and cultural) and in the sustainability of fishing or traditional cooking. This way of thinking influenced the output number 3 as the business plans are completely linked with sustainable and artisanal fishing practices.
The communication strategy was key to promote participation of fishing associations, find common visibility and identity of the project, establish protocols for publications and raise awareness about the project to reduce the security risks. Additional sessions of graphic design were held to create graphic identity of associations.
In order to attract young people an artistic contest Weaving Knowledge: Stories that link together and give life to artisanal fishing. 152 young between 14 to 23 years old of 6 schools presented drawings, couplets, poems that showed the views, stories and ideas that the young people of the municipality have regarding artisanal fishing in their territory. As award, the four winners went to the Gorgona national park, and all the proposals were exhibited in market square and town coliseum in Guapi. The embassy was part of the jury of this contest.
The dynamics of value creation and the characterization of the associations are linked to the third result. The team from Cauca's University of Economics and Lund University proposed a complete business plan for the commercialization of fresh, smoked and vacuum-packed fish to be sold in Guapi, Cali and Popayán. This includes supply and demand analysis, financial evaluation, cost and price analysis, feasibility studies and possible sources of financing. This is a technically and financially viable proposal that respects the social fabric and promotes community empowerment.
In addition to the previous achievements of the design team, with common visibility and identification of the project, last year the result was the creation of graphic identity of associations (Aservipesca and Renacer Progresista Guapireño) and a large mural (40mt2) painted on the wall of a school by many participants from the community. The mural contributes to dignify the fishing activity and to honor Hilario Caicedo, director of Aservipesca, who died in 2024.
Finally, regarding the second result, the structural design and manufacturing plans have been completed through an iterative process and with the active participation of the fishing association and a multidisciplinary team of naval engineers and designers from the National University and KTH. The proposed boat is a sailboat type, with a long keel of 12 mt, designed for river and sea fishing. The design responded to the following criteria: stability, safety, cost of construction and maintenance, ergonomic and fishing needs of the crew, environmental impact and cultural adaptation. Based on the prototype, the Unal received the authorization for construction from the Maritime and Port General Directorate (DIMAR is the Spanish acronym). The construction phase started in Buenaventura in the last quarter of 2024, including local materials for the hull that could guarantee replicability. The propulsion is mixed by the sail and a diesel Volvo Penta inboard engine donated by Chaneme (also a partner in the Ruta Motor program). It also has electrical and communication systems according to Colombian maritime regulations. An important advancement compared to the boats used by the artisanal fishermen in Guapi is the cabin. This prototype has a 6.5 mt2 cabin with a small kitchen, toilet, beds and storage space. The choice of the shipyard in Buenaventura was based on their long experience, proximity to Guapi and the possibility of building just one prototype.
The Embassy s assessment is that the universities have achieved important results until December 2024.
